Subject: Re: HIPAA / BAA eligibility - next steps

Hi Chris, great to meet today, thanks for walking us through MedWise's use case. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're all aligned: 

Summary of our conversation:
- Primary ask: confirm whether Redwood can support processing of PHI for MedWise's patient messaging and triage workflows.
- Key constraints you called out: BAA required, customer-managed KMS preferred, minimal data retention, and evidence for SOC 2 Type II.

What Redwood can offer (high-level):
- BAA: Redwood executes a Business Associate Agreement for eligible customers. We typically require either Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC / on-prem) deployment for PHI workloads.
- Hosted (multi-tenant) API: Not suitable for uncontrolled PHI by default. Hosted may be considered if the account is on a dedicated tenancy/reserved pool AND contractually covered by a BAA — we can discuss but it's uncommon for standard multi-tenant endpoints.
- PHI handling boundaries: for PHI workloads we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. We can support Customer-Managed Keys (KMS/HSM) in Private and in Dedicated where the deployment is provisioned in your VPC.
- Logging & retention: audit logs are available; retention policies can be scoped per-contract. For PHI we'll limit debug logging and can accommodate reduced retention windows.
- Caching & KV: you should plan to disable application-level prefix/KV caching for any input that contains PHI unless we add policy controls to ensure data is not persisted beyond the request (we'll document options).

Attachments included: Redwood_SOC2_Type2_2025_redacted.pdf, Redwood_BAA_FAQ.pdf — these should help legal and security triage.

Proposed next steps:
1) Please fill and return the vendor security questionnaire (I see Lara mentioned you'd attach it) — we included a slot for your SOC 2 + encryption KMS details.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Dev (cc'd) to map your data flow and confirm which deployment (Dedicated vs Private) fits your risk profile.
3) Legal: we can share a draft BAA after you confirm the preferred deployment model; I'll loop in our contracts rep once you confirm.

Would you be able to return the completed questionnaire by EOD next week (Sep 1)? If so, we'll fast-track the security review and get a draft BAA out within 3-5 business days after QA passes.

Thanks. I'll wait for the questionnaire and we can book the tech call.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Thanks Chris — answers inline below.

1) Hosted multi-tenant: public endpoints (shared tenancy) are not recommended for PHI. There are two paths that could make a hosted model acceptable: (a) we provision a Dedicated reserved pool tied to your account (effectively single-tenant capacity) and contractually extend the BAA to that deployment, or (b) a full Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) where you control the network boundary. For MedWise's goals (predictable throughput + PHI), Dedicated reserved capacity is the common choice and should meet your needs.

2) Caching controls: we support request-level controls to prevent persistent prefix/KV caching for particular routes; however, removing all caching behavior may require configuration of the serving profile at provisioning time for Dedicated. For Private deployments we can further restrict or disable caching and provide an operational runbook. Dev (cc'd) will cover specifics on the tech call.

3) Data deletion/retention: standard offering is configurable retention windows for request logs and audit trails. For PHI use-cases we can set a short retention SLA (e.g., 7-30 days) and exclude request bodies from long-term analytics. We'll include explicit retention language in the BAA draft.

Follow-ups I'll do this week:
- Share redacted SOC 2 (attached) and BAA FAQ (attached).
- Send a calendar invite for the tech deep-dive on Friday 8/28 9am PT — Dev, can you confirm?
- Once we receive the completed questionnaire, I'll route to Security for an expedited review and loop Legal for a draft BAA.

Dev/Neha — please review the attached questionnaire and be prepared to cover the deployment options & KMS integration on the call.

Thanks — looking forward to the call.

Best,
Marissa
